title: Filling a Mathlib TODO: JordanHolderLattice for Groups
content: This file fills an explicit gap in Mathlib: the concrete instance `JordanHolderLattice (Subgroup G)`. Mathlib's `Mathlib.Order.JordanHolder` defines the abstract `JordanHolderLattice` typeclass — a set of three lattice axioms sufficient to derive the Jordan-Hölder theorem — but deliberately leaves the group-theoretic instantiation as a TODO with the note 'it is not entirely clear how this should be done.' The difficulty lies in correctly handling quotient normal subgroup typeclasses in Lean 4, where the `Normal` instance for `G ⧸ H` depends inferentially on `H.Normal`, causing type-correct rewrites to fail. The file achieves: `sup_eq_of_isMaximal` and `second_iso` fully proved; one sorry remains in `isMaximal_inf_left_of_isMaximal_sup` (the maximality transfer step).
mathContext: The `JordanHolderLattice` typeclass requires three axioms for an ordered type $\alpha$: (1) $\text{IsMaximal}(x, z) \land \text{IsMaximal}(y, z) \land x \neq y \implies x \sqcup y = z$; (2) $\text{IsMaximal}(x, x \sqcup y) \land \text{IsMaximal}(y, x \sqcup y) \implies \text{IsMaximal}(x \sqcap y, x)$; (3) $\text{Iso}(x, x \sqcup y, x \sqcap y, y)$ (the second isomorphism). These axioms abstract the essential lattice properties needed to establish that composition factor multisets are unique.

title: IsMaxNorm: Maximal Normal Subgroup Predicate
content: `IsMaxNorm H K` captures the group-theoretic notion of H being maximal normal in K without requiring quotient types, sidestepping Lean's typeclass inference issues for `G ⧸ H`. It is logically equivalent to `IsSimpleGroup (K ⧸ H.subgroupOf K)` by the correspondence theorem — the composition factor is simple — but avoids quotient typeclass complications. The predicate has three components: strict inclusion `H < K`, relative normality `(H.subgroupOf K).Normal` (meaning every K-conjugate of H is again in H), and a maximality condition saying any relatively-normal-in-K subgroup between H and K must equal H or K.
mathContext: $\text{IsMaxNorm}(H, K)$ iff $H \lneq K$, $H \trianglelefteq K$ (relatively), and $\forall N.\, H \leq N \leq K \land N \trianglelefteq K \implies N = H \lor N = K$. This is equivalent to $K/H$ being simple (by the correspondence theorem), i.e., $K/H$ has no non-trivial normal subgroups. The reformulation avoids the Lean issue that `G ⧸ H` requires `H.Normal` as an inferred typeclass instance.

title: GroupQuotIso: Carrying Normality Evidence for Quotient Isomorphisms
content: `GroupQuotIso` encodes the equivalence relation on composition factors required by `JordanHolderLattice`. The key design choice is making the Normal witnesses explicit in the existential rather than relying on typeclass synthesis: the quotient type `G ⧸ H` requires `H.Normal` as a typeclass instance, and Lean may fail to synthesize this automatically when the subgroup expression is complex. By carrying `hn1` and `hn2` explicitly and introducing them with `haveI`, the definition ensures that quotient types are well-formed throughout the isomorphism construction.
mathContext: $\text{GroupQuotIso}((H_1, K_1), (H_2, K_2))$ asserts $\exists$ normality witnesses $\text{hn}_1, \text{hn}_2$ such that $K_1 / (H_1 \cap K_1) \cong K_2 / (H_2 \cap K_2)$ as groups. This formalizes the claim that composition factors at two steps in (possibly different) composition series are isomorphic, which is the core content of Jordan-Hölder uniqueness.

title: Normalizer Lemma: Normal-in-Sup Implies Normalizer Containment
content: This one-line lemma `le_normalizer_of_normal_in_sup` is used repeatedly: if H is relatively normal in H⊔K, then K lies inside the normalizer N_G(H). Intuitively, normality in the join means K-conjugates of H stay in H, which is exactly the definition of K ≤ N_G(H). In Lean 4, `normal_subgroupOf_iff_le_normalizer` connects relative normality of `H.subgroupOf (H ⊔ K)` to the normalizer inequality `H ⊔ K ≤ H.normalizer`, and then transitivity with `le_sup_right` extracts the K part.
mathContext: If $H \trianglelefteq H \vee K$ (relatively), then $K \leq N_G(H)$. Proof: `normal_subgroupOf_iff_le_normalizer` gives $H \vee K \leq N_G(H)$, and $K \leq H \vee K$ (by `le_sup_right`) gives the result by transitivity. This lemma is the key ingredient connecting the three JordanHolderLattice axioms.

title: sup_eq_of_isMaximal: Both Maximal Normal Implies Spanning Sup
content: This is the first and most conceptually transparent of the three Jordan-Hölder lattice axioms. If x and y are both maximal normal in z and x ≠ y, then x ⊔ y = z. The proof proceeds by showing x⊔y is relatively normal in z (using `subgroupOf_sup`, which distributes subgroupOf over sup, and then `infer_instance` for the product of normals). Then x's maximality condition says x⊔y = x or x⊔y = z. The case x⊔y = x means y ≤ x, and then y's maximality says y = x (contradicting x ≠ y) or y = z (contradicting y < z). So x⊔y = z.
mathContext: Given $x, y \trianglelefteq z$ both maximal and $x \neq y$: since $x \leq x \vee y \leq z$ and $x \vee y \trianglelefteq z$ (product of normals is normal), maximality of $x$ in $z$ gives $x \vee y = x$ or $x \vee y = z$. If $x \vee y = x$ then $y \leq x$, so maximality of $y$ gives $y = x$ (contradicts $x \neq y$) or $x = z$ (contradicts $x < z$). Hence $x \vee y = z$. Key Mathlib lemma: `subgroupOf_sup : (A \sqcup B).\text{subgroupOf}\, C = A.\text{subgroupOf}\, C \sqcup B.\text{subgroupOf}\, C`.

title: Diamond Argument: Transferring Maximality Through Intersection (Zassenhaus)
content: This is the hardest of the three axioms, and the source of the one remaining sorry. Given x and y both maximal normal in x⊔y, the goal is to show x⊓y is maximal normal in x. The proof establishes: (1) x⊓y < x (if x⊓y = x then x ≤ y, so x⊔y = y, contradicting y < x⊔y); (2) normality of (x⊓y).subgroupOf x (via the normalizer lemma and `inf_subgroupOf_right`). The hard third part — maximality — lifts a candidate N between x⊓y and x to N⊔y between y and x⊔y. Maximality of y gives N⊔y = y (so N ≤ y, hence N = x⊓y) or N⊔y = x⊔y (requiring simplicity transfer through second_iso, left as sorry).
mathContext: The Zassenhaus butterfly lemma: if $x, y \trianglelefteq x \vee y$ both maximal, then $x \wedge y \trianglelefteq x$ is maximal, with $(x \vee y)/y \cong x/(x \wedge y)$. The 'diamond' refers to the lattice: $x \wedge y < x, y < x \vee y$ forming a rhombus with isomorphic opposite quotients. The formal argument lifts $N$ (with $x \wedge y \leq N \leq x$) to $N \vee y$ in the $(y, x \vee y)$ interval, then applies maximality of $y$ to bifurcate: $N = x \wedge y$ or the hard case requiring simplicity transfer.

title: GroupQuotIso as an Equivalence Relation: Symmetry and Transitivity
content: `iso_symm` and `iso_trans` establish that `GroupQuotIso` is symmetric and transitive, as required by `JordanHolderLattice`. Both proofs pattern-match on the existential to extract Normal witnesses and equivalences, then use `MulEquiv.symm` (for symmetry) and `MulEquiv.trans` (for transitivity). The use of `Nonempty.map` for symmetry and explicit `rcases` for transitivity handles the propositional wrapping. These proofs are clean because `GroupQuotIso` was designed to carry the Normal witnesses explicitly.
mathContext: Symmetry: $K_1/H_1 \cong K_2/H_2 \implies K_2/H_2 \cong K_1/H_1$ via `MulEquiv.symm`. Transitivity: $K_1/H_1 \cong K_2/H_2$ and $K_2/H_2 \cong K_3/H_3$ implies $K_1/H_1 \cong K_3/H_3$ via `MulEquiv.trans`. Together with reflexivity (from the Jordan-Hölder machinery), these make `GroupQuotIso` an equivalence relation on composition factor pairs — the abstract sense in which factors are 'the same' across composition series.

title: Second Isomorphism via First Iso: Bypassing the sup_comm Rewrite Failure
content: The third and most technically subtle axiom: `second_iso` must prove `GroupQuotIso (x, x⊔y) (x⊓y, y)`, i.e., `(x⊔y)/x ≃* y/(x⊓y)`. The natural approach — apply `quotientInfEquivProdNormalizerQuotient` then rewrite `y⊔x = x⊔y` — fails in Lean 4: `rw [sup_comm y x]` gives 'motive not type correct' because the Normal typeclass instance for the quotient type depends on the term being rewritten. The fix constructs the isomorphism directly: define φ : y →* (x⊔y) ⧸ x.subgroupOf(x⊔y) as inclusion y ↪ x⊔y composed with the quotient map, prove ker φ = (x⊓y).subgroupOf y and surjectivity, then apply `quotientKerEquivOfSurjective`.
mathContext: Noether's second isomorphism: if $x \trianglelefteq x \vee y$, then $y/(x \wedge y) \cong (x \vee y)/x$. Direct proof: construct $\varphi: y \to (x \vee y)/x$ by $b \mapsto bx$, with $\ker \varphi = x \wedge y$ (elements of $y$ lying in $x$). Surjectivity: every coset $abx$ ($a \in x, b \in y$) equals $bx$ since $a$ cancels in the quotient. The first isomorphism theorem gives $y/\ker\varphi \cong (x \vee y)/x$. Taking `.symm` gives the required direction.

title: Jordan-Hölder Theorem: The Power of Abstract Typeclass Instantiation
content: The payoff: once `JordanHolderLattice (Subgroup G)` is established, the Jordan-Hölder theorem for groups is a one-liner delegating to Mathlib's abstract `CompositionSeries.jordan_holder`. This demonstrates the power of typeclass abstraction in Lean 4 — a single general proof works for groups, modules, and any structure satisfying the lattice axioms, simply by providing the appropriate instance. `jordan_holder_subgroups` asserts that any two composition series of G with the same endpoints are equivalent (same length, same composition factors up to permutation and isomorphism). `jordan_holder_finite_groups` adds the `[Finite G]` hypothesis for exposition.
mathContext: **Jordan-Hölder Theorem**: Let $G$ be a group with two composition series with the same endpoints. Then the series have the same length $n$ and there exists a permutation $\sigma$ such that $H_{i+1}/H_i \cong K_{\sigma(i)+1}/K_{\sigma(i)}$ for all $i$. In Lean: `CompositionSeries.Equivalent s₁ s₂` asserts a bijection between steps with pairwise `Iso`-related factors. Mathlib's abstract proof uses Wielandt's (1939) elegant induction, which is cleaner than the original arguments of Jordan (1870) and Hölder (1889) and works in any JordanHolderLattice.
